name: capcut-cli
use_label: Edit CapCut project drafts from a CLI
one_liner: An unofficial CLI that edits CapCut/JianYing project files directly on your machine — no upload, no account.

text.why: CapCut and JianYing normally mean clicking through the timeline by hand. capcut-cli reads and writes the local draft file (draft_content.json) directly, so cutting, captioning and speed changes become a one-line command or script — and the result still opens in CapCut with every track editable.
text.take: Working directly on a commercial editor's local files with no server is the hook; publicly disclosing and quickly patching its own security issues is what earns the trust.
build: A zero-dependency Node.js CLI that works directly on the local draft store — no server, no upload. Whisper and FFmpeg plug in optionally for captions and rendering, and it installs as an agent skill for Claude Code, Codex and others.

who.role: Editors churning out short-form video in CapCut/JianYing at volume, and anyone who wants to script captioning and cutting.

start.text: Install with npm install -g capcut-cli, then run capcut quickstart my-first --video clip.mp4 and open the result in CapCut.

caveat: The README states clearly it is an independent project, not affiliated with ByteDance. Versions up to 0.17.0 had a local command-injection issue, and up to 0.17.2 could leak a device identifier — use 0.18.0 or later.

license.scope_text: Use, change and redistribute, commercially too. Keep the notice.

numbers.star_delta_unit: GitHub stars gained in the window, GH Archive events summed to as_of
numbers.method: Star total = the value last checked on GitHub (stars_checked_at) + increases observed via GH Archive since. The 24h · 7d · 30d gains are GH Archive hourly events summed to the reference time (as_of). No score of ours.
